Storage, diagnostics and performance

Source: vignettes/performance.Rmd
performance.Rmd

The fold object keeps canonical data and compressed indices. Contiguous temporal memberships use shared ordering and range endpoints; repeated spatial/taxon sets share membership definitions. Fixed-station space-time queries search temporal intervals for neighbouring station geometries. Analysis sets are complements and are not stored as duplicated vectors.

x <- tibble::tibble(time = seq_len(1000))
folds <- neighbourhoods(x,
  index = time,
  temporal = temporal_window(time_span(3, "seconds"))
)
print(folds)
#> <naboer_folds: neighbourhood>
#> 1,000 observations; 1,000 folds
tibble::as_tibble(folds, folds = c(1, 500, 1000))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#>   fold  n_assessment n_omission n_analysis n_buffer omitted_fraction
#>   <chr>        <dbl>      <dbl>      <dbl>    <dbl>            <dbl>
#> 1 1                1          4        996        3            0.004
#> 2 500              1          7        993        6            0.007
#> 3 1000             1          4        996        3            0.004
diagnostics <- summary(folds)
diagnostics[c("assessment_size", "omission_size", "omitted_fraction", "unassessed")]
#> $assessment_size
#> [1] 1 1
#> 
#> $omission_size
#> [1] 4 7
#> 
#> $omitted_fraction
#> [1] 0.004 0.007
#> 
#> $unassessed
#> [1] 0

as_tibble() omits membership list-columns unless membership = TRUE. assessment_indices(), omission_indices() and analysis_indices() expand only requested folds; asking for all folds is explicit but can consume large amounts of memory. summary() reports assessment coverage without retaining expanded memberships. Plot selected folds with ggplot2::autoplot(folds, folds = 1).

Materialising nei

mgcv consumes packed observation indices. This output is proportional to the total membership count even when the fold object is compact. Export checks the integer-index limit and estimates output bytes before allocation. The default 1 GiB guard can be adjusted explicitly:

nei <- as_nei(folds, max_bytes = 100 * 1024^2)
sum(vapply(nei, length, integer(1)))
#> [1] 9988

The estimate covers packed integer arrays, not the total R process or temporary allocation peaks. Use a limit below available memory. Sampling bam neighbourhood criteria does not remove the requirement to define all neighbourhoods. Forecast designs retain compressed future exclusions until export, which can itself be quadratic in the number of observations/origins.

Reproducible benchmarks

The source repository’s benchmarks/ directory contains R scripts for million-row multiple-series data, fixed monitoring stations, moving locations, polygons and approximation studies. They are excluded from routine CRAN tests. Records should include input dimensions, memberships, compressed/output sizes, runtime, R heap high-water or process peak memory (clearly distinguished), hardware, R/dependency versions and brute-force agreement on sampled focal observations.

Dense windows are deliberately tested with preallocation guards. A sparse million-row design and a dense million-row design have very different output costs; construction runtime does not predict packed size.
